newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates ease slightly on HKMA injection.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates ease slightly on HKMA injection.

text.p: Hong Kong interbank rates eased slightly on Monday after the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) injected HK$200 million into the market to soothe tight liquidity, dealers said.
Overnight cash eased to 5-1/4 1/8 percent from 5-5/16 1/4 at midday on Friday and three-month money traded at 5-1/2 3/8 percent versus 5-9/16 1/2.
"The overnight surged to a high of 5-3/8 percent, then moved back to 5-3/16 after the injection, but it is still higher than in Friday afternoon," a Japanese bank dealer said.
The HKMA has pumped a total of HK$407 million into the market in the past five days due to tight liquidity.
Dealers said short-term liquidity was squeezed by a number of initial public offerings (IPO) and rights issues.
"I believe the short-term rate has room to go up by 1/16 as the month-end is approaching," the Japanese bank dealer said.
In bills and notes market, yields of short-dated government papers eased in line with the cash market. The one-week Exchange Fund bill yielded 4.86 percent versus 4.95 at Friday midsession.
Three-year notes yielded 6.32 percent versus 6.38, five-year notes yielded 6.90 percent versus 6.95, and seven-year notes yielded 7.27 percent versus 7.31.
Dealers said trading was featureless with all eyes on U.S. economic figures due later this week.
